neighbours.label: concrete noun object of a preposition in narrative description (the picture, the heavy night air, power lines, sediment)
fire: The monks allowed him to carry it close to the picture of the saint.
A loud report rolled far through the heavy night air.
A gull flew into two power lines near the harbour on Tuesday.
The finest particles take decades to settle into sediment.
Smoke drifted slowly over the trees at the edge of the field.
The kite became tangled among the clouds of dust above the road.
Rain dripped steadily from the posts of the old fence.
Children hung their coats beneath the picture of the queen.
quiet: The monks allowed him to stay for a while longer.
A loud report rolled far and was soon forgotten.
A gull flew away quickly near the harbour on Tuesday.
The finest particles take decades to settle completely.
Smoke drifted slowly and then disappeared entirely.
The kite became tangled and came down near the road.
Rain dripped steadily for most of the afternoon.
Children hung their coats and went in to lunch.
